2016 Agreement: The Victorian Public Services Mental Health Enterprise Agreement 2016-2020.
2020 Agreement: The Victorian Public Services Mental Health Enterprise Agreement 2020-2024.
Adoption: Includes the placement of a Child by permanent care order, and kinship care where it is comparable to adoption, having regard for all the circumstances.
Allied Health Professional: A person employed in any of the classifications set out in Schedule 5 of this Agreement, excluding Lived and Living Experience Workers.
Bank Employee: A directly employed casual Employee engaged in relieving work of a casual nature.
CATT: Crisis Assessment Treatment Team — includes other community-based crisis response work designated by the Employer, however titled.
Commission: The Fair Work Commission or any successor body.
Consumer Consultant: A person employed and classified as a Consumer Consultant in Schedule 5, Part 5, Clause 4.2. Does not include persons who volunteer as consumer consultants.
Department: The Department of Health (Victoria) or any of its predecessors or successors.
Employee: A person employed by an Employer and engaged solely or predominantly in the provision of Mental Health Services, in a classification/occupation within the Agreement.
Employer: Any of the employers listed in Schedule 1 of this Agreement.
Family Carer Consultant: A person employed and classified as a Family Carer Consultant in Schedule 5, Part 5, Clause 4.2. Does not include persons who volunteer as family carer consultants.
FFPPOA: First full pay period on or after.
HACSU: Health and Community Services Union — a Branch of the Health Services Union.
HRP Act: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law Act 2009 (Vic).
Immediate Family: A spouse, former spouse, de facto partner, former de facto partner, child, parent, grandparent, grandchild, or sibling of the Employee or their spouse/de facto partner; includes step and adoptive relations.
Lived and Living Experience Worker: An Employee employed in accordance with the definition in Schedule 5.
Management and Administrative Officer: A person employed in any of the classifications listed in Schedule 7 of this Agreement.
Mental Health Services/Psychiatric Servi: The delivery of human services concerned with the prevention of mental illness and the assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, maintenance and support of those persons who may be at risk of or suffering from mental illness or psychiatric disability by Employers listed in Schedule 1.
MHIIC: Mental Health Industry Implementation Committee — the committee referred to in clause 12.1.
MHO: Mental Health Officer — a person employed and classified in accordance with the MHO classification in clause 110.
NES: National Employment Standards as contained in the Fair Work Act 2009.
NMBA: Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia.
Peer Worker: A person employed and classified as a Peer Worker in Schedule 5, Part 5. Does not include persons who volunteer as Peer Support Workers.
PEN: Psychiatric Enrolled Nurse — a person classified under clause 109, registered as an Enrolled Nurse in Division 2 on the Register of Nurses of the NMBA.
Pool Employee: A class of non-casual Employees who agree to be available for deployment across all or part of a Health Service.
Relevant qualification: A qualification or certificate (including components thereof) or course of study considered relevant based on: (a) the nature of the education and the Employee's current area of practice; and (b) other factors including clinical area of work, classification, position description, and whether the education would assist the Employee in performing their role.
RPN: Registered Psychiatric Nurse — a person classified under clause 108, registered as a Registered Nurse in the Register of Nurses of the NMBA.
Support Services Employee: A person employed in any of the classifications listed in Schedule 6 of this Agreement.
VHIA: Victorian Hospitals' Industrial Association — the employers' representative body.
WIC: Workplace Implementation Committee — the committee referred to in clause 12.3.
WIRC Act: Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 (Vic), or where applicable the Accident Compensation Act 1985 (Vic) or the Workers Compensation Act 1958 (Vic).
